name: Bunny "Striker" Lee
hook: The most prolific producer in 1970s reggae, whose sheer volume of studio time gave King Tubby the raw material to invent the remix.

blurb.age7: Bunny Lee made more reggae records than almost anyone in the 1970s, and King Tubby turned many of them into dub versions.
blurb.age13: Edward "Bunny" Lee started as a record plugger before producing his first hit in 1967. Through the 1970s he was reggae's most prolific producer, working constantly with engineer King Tubby, whose dub remixes of Lee's productions helped turn dub into a genre.
blurb.adult: Lee (born Edward O'Sullivan Lee) entered the industry in 1962 as a plugger for Duke Reid's Treasure Isle label before producing his own first hit, Roy Shirley's 'Music Field,' in 1967. His prolific 1970s output, especially with singers Johnny Clarke and Cornell Campbell, gave King Tubby the sheer volume of raw material that let dub develop into a genre rather than a one-off technique.

signatureTracks.title: The Gorgon (Cornell Campbell)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: A Lee production that launched a wave of like-minded 'Gorgon rock' records, showing how one hit could set a template others copied for years.

signatureTracks.title: None Shall Escape the Judgement (Johnny Clarke)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Part of the Lee/Clarke run of roots hits that, alongside Tubby's dub cuts of the same rhythms, defined mid-1970s Jamaican radio.
